items.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 25 at 3:14AM EST until November 26 at 5:00PM EST by NWS Wakefield VA
items.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10 to
17 feet expected in the surf zone. For the Coastal Flood
Warning, 2 to 4 feet of inundation above ground level expected
in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...In Maryland, Maryland Beaches. In Virginia, Accomack and
Northampton.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, from 10 AM this morning to
7 AM EST Friday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 5 AM to 5
PM EST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Major flooding is expected resulting in extreme
inundation. Water will be 2 to 4 feet or more above ground level
in flooded areas. Numerous homes and businesses could be
flooded. Many roads across the area may become impassable for an
extended period of time causing many neighborhoods to become
flooded and isolated. Life threatening flooding will extend well
inland from the waterfront and shoreline. Should evacuations
become necessary, follow the advice of local officials for
evacuation information.
items.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

items.headline: Flood Watch issued November 25 at 1:49AM EST until November 26 at 4:00PM EST by NWS Wakefield VA
items.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Portions of southeast Maryland, including the following
areas, Dorchester, Inland Worcester, Maryland Beaches, Somerset and
Wicomico and Virginia, including the following areas, Accomack,
Eastern Essex, Eastern King William, Eastern King and Queen,
Gloucester, Lancaster, Mathews, Middlesex, Northampton,
Northumberland, Richmond, Western Essex, Western King William,
Western King and Queen and Westmoreland.

* WHEN...From this evening through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Storm drains
and ditches may become clogged with debris.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Strong low pressure lifts northward late tonight into the
Thanksgiving holiday. Widespread moderate to locally heavy
rainfall is expected over much of the area.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
items.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

items.headline: High Wind Warning issued November 25 at 1:34AM EST until November 26 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Wakefield VA
items.description:
* WHAT...East winds 30 to 45 mph with gusts up to 60 mph expected. A
few wind gusts may exceed 60 mph along the immediate coast.

* WHERE...In Maryland, the Maryland beaches, Dorchester, Inland
Worcester, Somerset, and Wicomico Counties. In Virginia,
Northampton and Accomack Counties.

* WHEN...From 10 PM this evening to 7 PM EST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Damaging winds will blow down trees and power lines.
Widespread power outages are expected. Travel will be difficult,
especially for high profile vehicles.
items.instruction:
People are urged to secure loose objects that could be blown around
or damaged by the wind.

items.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued November 25 at 2:09AM EST until November 25 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Wakefield VA
items.description:
* WHAT...For the Small Craft Advisory, northeast winds 20 to 25
kt with gusts up to 30 kt and seas 7 to 10 ft. For the Storm
Warning, east winds 30 to 40 kt with gusts up to 55 kt and seas
17 to 22 ft expected.

* WHERE...Coastal waters from Fenwick Island DE to Chincoteague
VA out 20 NM and Coastal waters from Chincoteague to Parramore
Island VA out 20 NM.

* WHEN...For the Small Craft Advisory, until 7 PM EST this
evening. For the Storm Warning, from 7 PM this evening to 7 PM
EST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Storm force winds and hazardous seas will capsize or
damage vessels and reduce visibility.
items.instruction:
Mariners should remain in port, alter course, and/or secure the
vessel for severe conditions.
